title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p.629). Grothendieck compares the moduli stack M_{1,1} with a coarser object M'_{1,1}. The latter is linked to U_{0,3} = M_{0,3} = P^1 minus {0,1,infinity} through the S_3 = SL(2,Z)/Gamma(2) action. He uses a central extension 1 -> mu = {+-1} -> S~_3 = SL(2,Z)/M -> S_3 -> 1, where M is a normal subgroup of Gamma(2) not containing -1.

(1) The rational point. A Q-rational point of M'_{1,1} gives an S_3-torsor T, equivalently a homomorphism Pi_Q -> S_3. Lifts of the point to M_{1,1} correspond to S~_3-torsors lifting T, i.e. lifts Pi_Q -> S~_3. The obstruction lies in H^2(Q, mu_2) = 2Br(Q).

(2) The point j=0. Here the fibre in M_{0,3} is {-j, -j-bar}, the roots of lambda^2 - lambda + 1. Galois acts through Gal(Q(j)/Q), where Q(j) = Q(cube roots of 1) = Q(sqrt -3). The image of Galois in S_3 is the order-2 subgroup {1, sigma_infinity-dot}. The reason given: tau' = sigma.tau, tau and 1 all map to sigma_infinity-dot. Hence T = T_0 wedge^{mu} S_3 is induced from the mu-torsor T_0 = Spec Q(sqrt -3) via mu -> S_3, -1 |-> sigma_infinity-dot.

(3) Reduction to Z/4. The preimage of {1, sigma_infinity-dot} in S~_3 is an extension E'' of mu by mu. The margin justifies E'' = Z/4 canonically: the image of the matrix S = [[0,-1],[1,0]] has order 4 in SL(2,Z)/M because -1 is not in M. So S~_3 is the binary dihedral (dicyclic) group of order 12. The lifting problem therefore reduces to the classical embedding problem: lift the quadratic character chi of Q(sqrt -3) through Z/4 -> Z/2. The obstruction is chi^*(E''), i.e. chi cup chi = (-3,-3) = (-1,-3) in Br_2(Q).

(4) The obstruction is nonzero. Bottom-left margin: any lift to Z/4 is abelian, so it factors through (Pi_Q)^ab = Z^*-hat. The character chi lives on the Z_3^* factor through its torsion (Z_3^*)_tors = Z/2. Z_3^* = mu_2 x (1+3Z_3) has no finite-order character psi with psi^2 nontrivial on mu_2. Hence no lift exists.

(5) Consequence (next page). The rational point j=0 of M'_{1,1} does not lift to a Q-rational point of M_{1,1}. Its image in U_{0,3}/S_3 should still lift in a suitable sense, which he then studies.
errors: No mathematical error detected. The conclusion is correct: Q(sqrt -3) does not embed in a cyclic quartic field because -3 is not a sum of two squares. The quaternion algebra (-1,-3) is ramified at 3 and infinity.
Minor: the role of M (which normal subgroup of Gamma(2)) is not specified on this page, so the identification of S~_3 with Dic_3 is inferred.

ideas.what: Rational points of a coarse/rigidified moduli space lift to the stack iff the associated Galois representation lifts through a central extension. The obstruction is a class in 2Br(Q).
ideas.modern_name: Gerbe obstruction / field of moduli vs field of definition via central extension (lifting problem in Galois cohomology)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Giraud (non-abelian cohomology, 1971); Serre (Witt-invariant formula, 1984); Debes-Douai and others for fields of moduli
ideas.where_published: Spirit present in SGA1 / Esquisse d'un programme discussions of Galois action on M_{g,n}; this specific computation is unpublished

ideas.what: Preimage of a transposition in SL(2,Z)/M is Z/4, generated by the image of S, so the lifting problem becomes a Z/4 embedding problem.
ideas.modern_name: Binary dihedral group Dic_3 as a central extension of S_3 = SL_2(F_2); cyclic quartic embedding problem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (embedding problems: Witt 1936; Q(sqrt d) is in a C4-extension iff d is a sum of two squares)

ideas.what: Abelianization argument: obstruction is non-zero because Z_3^* has no character squaring to the nontrivial character of its torsion.
ideas.modern_name: Class field theory / local character computation

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, correct worked example: the j=0 point of a coarse M_{1,1}-type quotient fails to lift because of the cyclic-quartic embedding obstruction (-1,-3). The method and result are classical in substance (Witt-type embedding problems, gerbe obstructions); only the specific instance inside Grothendieck's 'equation des lacets' study is unpublished.
transcription_corrections: '619' at top is Grothendieck's own page numbering (archive page 630).
'que j'ai noté des notes' is likely 'que j'ai notée' followed by the symbol E'' (i.e. 'que j'ai noté E'''), with Z/4Z written above it.
'[illisible] cocaiste sûrement posé' probably reads '(problème classique sûrement posé)'.
Bottom-left margin: likely 'c'est évident, puisque (Pi_Q)_ab = Z^*-hat contains Z_3^*, et (Z_3^*)_tors = Z/2Z ... on ne peut relever ...' — an argument that the character on Z_3^* cannot lift to Z/4.
Top-left margin: 'oui, c'est évident puisque sigma = sigma_infinity dans S~_3 = SL(2,Z)/M est bien d'ordre 4, donc E'' = Z/4Z canoniquement'.
